collections.description: The Liferay Sites Design System (https://makenaford.github.io/liferay-sites-design-system) as plain Liferay fragments: the simplest story of each component, with its basic props as configuration and its content as editables. The design tokens live in the "Classic + Liferay Sites DS" theme and its LSDS Dark / LSDS Light style books. Generated by scripts/build-lsds.mjs.

fragments.docs: Banner A full-width strip with a title, a sentence and one action. It closes a page or breaks a long sequence of sections. Tone and alignment brand and accent are both gradients and look alike on purpose: the design system keeps them for pages that alternate two banners. neutral is the flat version for quieter pages. Left alignment is for banners that sit under a left-aligned section; centred is the default closing banner. Writing One sentence, one verb, one action. The rich text (text-2) accepts bold and links, but a banner with a paragraph in it has stopped being a banner.
fragments.name: LSDS Banner

fragments.docs: Button The primary call to action of the Liferay Sites design system. One fragment, four variants and three sizes, all driven by configuration.json, so an editor picks them from the fragment's panel and never touches markup. When to use each variant - filled is the one action a block exists for: the hero's "Contact sales", a section's "See all resources". One per block. - outline sits next to a filled button as the secondary path, "Watch the demo" beside "Start free". - neutral is for actions on media or dark surfaces where brand colour would compete with the content. - rounded is the pill shape the marketing pages use in navigation and chips. Do not mix it with the other shapes in the same block. Sizes lg is the default on pages, md inside cards and forms, sm only in dense places such as the header. In Liferay The link is an editable (link-1), so the text and the target are mapped in the page editor like any Liferay link: a URL, a page or a content field. The button renders as an <a on purpose: Liferay cannot map a <button. Tokens it reads: --sds-btn- for the shape and --sds-action- for the colours, both in the style books.
fragments.name: LSDS Button

fragments.docs: Card The unit of every grid on the marketing pages: a resource, a capability, a customer story. Image, label, title, text and a link, each an editable. Surfaces - glass is the default on the dark pages, a translucent panel over the gradient. - static is the flat card for light pages and dense grids. - highlighted singles out one card in a row, the featured resource. - none drops the panel and keeps only the content, for image-led grids. Tone blue and purple set the accent of the label and the hover glow; they do not change the surface. Use one tone per grid. In Liferay The image (image-1) and the link (link-1) are the usual editables, which is what makes a card mappable to a content set: drop the card in a collection display, map the image and the title to the content fields, and the grid fills itself.
fragments.name: LSDS Card

fragments.docs: Hero The first block of every page: an eyebrow, a title, a sentence and two actions. It has no configuration on purpose, so every page opens the same way and the variation lives in the words and the media. Editables | Id | Type | Use | | --- | --- | --- | | text-1 | text | The eyebrow, one or two words | | title-1 | text | The title, two lines at most on desktop | | text-2 | text | The sentence under the title | | link-1 | link | The primary action, a filled button | | link-2 | link | The secondary action, an outline button | In a page On LSDS Home the hero sits under the fixed header, and the header's height is accounted for by the hero's own padding (body:has(.headerShell[data-position=fixed])). When you compose a page without the header, the hero keeps a smaller top padding.
fragments.name: LSDS Hero

fragments.docs: Label A short tag over a title: the type of a resource, the state of a feature, the category of a card. Labels never carry an action. Variants - gradient is the default and the only one to use on light surfaces. - glass is for media and the dark hero, where the label floats over an image. - filled is for tonal surfaces such as cards and banners. Keep the text to one or two words. A label that wraps is a label that should have been a paragraph. Colours The text colour is --sds-surfaces-text-primary in every variant, so a label is readable on the light and the dark style books without a variant switch. Compare it by changing the style book in the toolbar.
fragments.name: LSDS Label

fragments.docs: Section: Resources A section title, an intro and a grid of three resource cards, each with a label, an image and a title. It is the section of a page that most often becomes a collection display in Liferay. Structure The section is one fragment so that an editor can drop it as a whole; inside, every card repeats the Card pattern with its own editables (image-1, text-2, text-3...). For a grid fed by content, use the Card fragment inside a collection display instead and keep this section for hand-picked resources. Labels The labels in the cards use the gradient variant of Label; change the style book to LSDS Light in the toolbar to see them keep their contrast.
fragments.name: LSDS Section: Resources

docs.text: Getting started This site is the published, versioned face of a set of Liferay assets: fragment sets, page templates and style books. Everything you see here is exactly what gets imported into Liferay, rendered without a Liferay. What is here - Fragments, grouped in fragment sets. Each one renders live with its configuration as controls and its editables as fields, like the fragment panel in the page editor. - Page templates, composed of those fragments with Liferay's own layout structure (containers, rows, columns). - Style books, the sets of token values a theme exposes. Switch one in the toolbar and every fragment and page restyles. - Docs, these pages and the Docs tab of each fragment, written in plain Markdown next to the asset. - Releases, one per version, with the zips and the exact list of assets that changed. Import into Liferay Every asset exports as the zip Liferay imports, from the same place you see it: 1. A fragment set: the download icon next to the set in the sidebar. Import it in Site Builder → Fragments → Import. Fragments keep their key, so a newer version updates the fragments in place. 2. One fragment: Export fragment in the toolbar. It is a one-fragment set. 3. A page template: Export template in the toolbar, then Site Builder → Page Templates → Import. The page-definition.json button gives the definition alone, for the headless API or for an agent. 4. A style book: the download icon in the style book group of the toolbar, then Site Builder → Style Books → Import. Each release lists the same zips attached to the GitHub release, so a team imports a version, not a snapshot of someone's browser. Bring your own assets Drop any Liferay export on the page: a fragment set, a page template, a style book, a built theme, or a bare page-definition.json. Imported assets stay in your browser and never leave it. Where the files live The folders are the Liferay export layout, so a Liferay export unzips straight into the repository and a release is a tag.
docs.title: Getting started

docs.text: Page composition A page template is Liferay's page-definition.json: a tree of containers, rows and columns with fragments in them. The Layout tab under a template edits that tree directly, and the export is the zip Liferay imports. LSDS Home The home page of the design system, every block a fragment of the "Liferay Sites DS pages" set. Composing a page 1. New in the Page templates section of the sidebar. 2. In the Layout tab, add a Container (full width or fluid), a Row with the columns you need, and a Fragment in each column from the picker. 3. Click any element in the preview or in the tree to edit its styles: spacing, background, borders, the same options as the page editor, stored in fragmentStyle with the theme's spacer tokens. 4. Export template, or copy page-definition.json from the Code tab. For agents The page-definition.json format is stable and documented in the AI catalog at /catalog.json and /llms.txt. An agent that reads the catalog can compose a page from the fragment keys and hand back a definition; drop that file on this site and it becomes a template you can review, edit and export. docs.text: Tokens and style books The design system's tokens are not a separate file: they are Liferay frontend tokens, declared by the theme and valued by style books. That is what lets one fragment set serve a light and a dark site with no change to the fragments. How it fits together - The theme (Classic + Liferay Sites DS) declares every token with its CSS variable and default value, in frontend-token-definition.json. - A style book overrides values. LSDS Light and LSDS Dark are two style books of the same theme. - A fragment reads CSS variables only, never colours. var(--sds-surfaces-text-primary) is the whole contract. Switch the style book in the toolbar: the tables below and every embedded preview follow it. Brand and accent Surfaces and text These are the tokens most fragments read. Text primary is what labels, titles and body text use on every surface. Actions Buttons and links. Sizes and spacing Editing a style book Create or duplicate a style book from the toolbar, edit any token in the Style book tab under a fragment, and export it. The export is the zip Liferay's Style Books admin imports, and it keeps a reference to the theme it belongs to.
docs.title: Tokens and style books

pageDefinition.description: A page template is a Liferay page-definition.json: {"pageElement": <Root>, "version": 1.1}. Element types nest Root > Section > Container > Row > Column > Fragment. A Fragment element is {"type": "Fragment", "definition": {"fragment": {"collectionKey": "<collection key>", "key": "<fragment key>"}, "fragmentConfig": {<configuration name>: <value>}, "fragmentFields": [{"id": "<editable id>", "value": {"text": {"value_i18n": {"en_US": "<text>"}}}}]}}. For a link editable the value is {"text": {"value_i18n": {"en_US": "<label>"}}, "fragmentLink": {"value": {"href": {"value_i18n": {"en_US": "<url>"}}}}}; for an image, {"fragmentImage": {"url": {"value": "<src>"}}}. A Row is {"type": "Row", "definition": {"numberOfColumns": N}, "pageElements": [{"type": "Column", "definition": {"size": 12/N}, "pageElements": [...]}]}. Drop the JSON file on the site, or import it through the Liferay headless API.
